title: Hospital levy referred to 2027 budget
subtitle: Also: RetrofitWR fee exemptions, Doon Pioneer Village admission options, and a closed session on land, prosecutions and airport lease.
overview: The Administration and Finance Committee dealt mainly with a proposed special levy to start saving for the local share of the future Waterloo Region Health Network (WRHN) hospital and Cambridge hospital projects. The original motion, equal to 0.5% of the annual tax-supported budget, was not voted on as written. Instead the committee recommended referring the levy idea to staff for the 2027 base budget cycle, whether or not the province and WRHN have confirmed a final dollar amount {{vote:m4}}. This matters because any levy would affect future property tax bills.

On the consent agenda, the committee recommended exemptions from the RetrofitWR program administration fee: a permanent one for income-eligible households and a temporary one for the first 50 other households {{vote:m1}}. Committee also asked staff to report to the May Council meeting on admission options, including waiving the two dollar fee or pay-what-you-can, for the Doon Pioneer Village re-opening event.

The committee then met in closed session on a proposed land acquisition in Cambridge, Provincial Offences Act prosecutions, a possible airport land lease and Unifor Local 4304 negotiations. The minutes report no decisions from it. The next meeting is June 2, 2026.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended referring a special hospital local share levy of 0.5% of the tax-supported budget to staff for the 2027 base budget, regardless of whether a final amount is confirmed by WRHN or the province.
The committee recommended a permanent exemption from the $450 RetrofitWR program administration fee for income-eligible households to improve program equity.
The committee recommended a temporary exemption from the $450 administration fee for the first 50 non-income-eligible households to support early program uptake.
The committee received the consent agenda items for information and approved them, including the RetrofitWR report {{vote:m1}}.

debate: Supporters of the levy said saving now is sound financial practice because a very large local share is coming, and earlier saving lets invested funds earn interest, reducing the future tax burden. The mover said the 0.5% would not raise the full amount even over several years.

Some councillors questioned the timing and the lack of numbers. They said the levy would take effect under the next council, and that WRHN and the Cambridge hospital board should present expected asks first. Another councillor said hospital boards may not give a figure for years, so waiting is not practical.

Several councillors wanted Cambridge Memorial and the other existing hospital sites treated fairly and sequenced alongside the new hospital. The mover noted the fund would cover both the new hospital and Cambridge projects.

The chair asked that the staff report look at what area municipalities and other Ontario communities have contributed to hospital projects. Another councillor said the specialty services draw patients from well beyond the region. A third said the money comes from the same taxpayers whichever tax base is used.

On Doon Pioneer Village, one councillor favoured pay-what-you-can, while another worried it could embarrass families. A third said the two dollar fee returns to the original rate and suggested staff discretion for those who cannot pay.
